## Summary

Add opt-in, bounded admission for CUDA IPC/VMM feature publication. Related to #43402; this does **not** claim to fix its CUDA-driver hang or bound upstream GPU preprocessing.

- Reserve the whole publication batch atomically (including alignment, fragmentation and IPC control slots); wait without holding partial slices or occupying the copy worker.
- `--mm-admission-timeout-ms 0` rejects on pressure; positive values wait up to the deadline. Oversized batches return 413, temporary pressure 429. HTTP/OpenAI/SSE and Python/Rust gRPC preserve these errors.
- Keep reservations and source ownership until native copy completion, including cancellation and failed dispatch. Preserve generation/ACK semantics and existing VMM packing.
- Add pool/pending/lease-lifetime diagnostics and concise VLM/argument/K3 documentation.

Unset preserves existing behavior. No default transport/backend change, extra HBM pool, silent CPU fallback on the guarded path, or EPD/PD support.

## Development validation

Isolated NVIDIA B200, driver 580.126.09, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0; production head `db2fb5d0a319a3c4cac2734315c414c166bf69ac`:

- 661 CPU tests + 494 subtests and 10 CUDA IPC / single-device POSIX-VMM tests passed (exit 0). A CUDA IPC process-teardown warning remains recorded, not claimed resolved.
- Python gRPC boundary tests and 19 Rust `sglang-grpc` tests passed; workspace Clippy passed with the pinned Rust toolchain. Subsequent changes do not modify Rust/gRPC code.
- Real-weight Qwen2.5-VL-3B (revision `66285546d2b821cf421d4f5eb2576359d3770cd3`) IPC and Qwen3-VL-2B (`89644892e4d85e24eaac8bacfd4f463576704203`) POSIX VMM: normal requests, multi-image/color checks, 413/429 under a 2 MiB pool, idle drain and successful recovery passed.
- Both transports passed three 16-request rounds of actual abort, pool/pending drain, cache flush and a successful subsequent image request.
- Cookbook configuration, MDX build and link validation passed.

### Performance gate — draft, not a recommended default

Same-commit opt-in/off IPC replay: 64 MiB pool, cache off, CUDA graphs off, 448-square image, up to 8 output tokens, concurrency 1/8. Per mode: 96 warmups per concurrency, then 3 x 256 measured requests per concurrency; all 1,539 recorded requests succeeded, plus 192 unrecorded warmups.

Guarded-first order at `db2fb5d0`:

| Concurrency | Legacy median RPS (range) | Guarded median RPS (range) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 24.341 (24.202–24.514) | 24.252 (24.156–24.572) |
| 8 | 112.907 (112.402–116.162) | 102.148 (101.094–110.191) |

Concurrency-8 throughput regresses about 9.53%; an earlier legacy-first replay also regressed. This exceeds the 3% acceptance target and remains a merge-readiness gate. These are E2E serving measurements, not TTFT or a universal speedup claim.

A second matched replay with two processor workers per mode also completed with all requests successful: concurrency-8 median 108.890 RPS (104.738–110.196) legacy vs 104.826 RPS (98.377–105.975) guarded, a 3.73% regression. Increasing processor concurrency does not establish that the performance gate is met, and does not replace the default-worker result above.

Not validated: full Kimi-K3, multi-node FABRIC/MNNVL, multi-tokenizer-worker/session serving, or incident-shaped long soak. Pre-decode/native-memory budgeting remains a separate follow-up; accounting only torch tensors would miss native decoder workspace.

## CI

Exact-head targeted runs passed: [CPU — 9 test files](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41328781136), [IPC/H100 — 9 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41328791322), [VMM/GB300 — 16 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41328801373). The GPU tests actually ran, including FABRIC round-trip/recycling and guarded single-device POSIX-VMM pressure/reclaim; this is not two-node serving validation. [Rust workspace](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41328743237), [lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41328694316), title and documentation checks also passed. No full unrelated matrix was requested; automatic Base/Extra gate failures are expected while this remains a draft without `run-ci`. The performance and broader validation gates above remain open.

 For multimodal models, you can use `--mm-feature-transport=cuda_ipc` to optimize for latency at the cost of increased GPU memory usage:
 
-- **Default behavior**: Multimodal feature tensors are moved to CPU after processing to save GPU memory
+- **CPU transport**: Multimodal feature tensors are moved to CPU after processing. Automatic transport selection depends on the model and topology; use `--mm-feature-transport cpu` to select this explicitly.
 - **With `--mm-feature-transport=cuda_ipc`**: Feature tensors stay in a bounded GPU pool shared over CUDA IPC, reducing device-to-host copy overhead and improving latency, but consuming more GPU memory
 
 Use this option when you have sufficient GPU memory and want to minimize latency for multimodal inference.
 
+### GPU feature-pool admission
+
+On NVIDIA CUDA, normal serving can opt into `--mm-admission-timeout-ms` with
+`--mm-feature-transport cuda_ipc` or `cuda_vmm`. This protects publication into
+the feature pool; it does **not** bound image decoding or preprocessing memory,
+and is not a fix for a CUDA driver hang.
+
+- Unset: keep the existing per-tensor CPU fallback when the pool is full.
+- `0`: reject immediately if the whole publication batch cannot fit now.
+- Positive: wait up to that many milliseconds for pool capacity, then reject.
+
+The publisher reserves all required slices before copying. Waiting requests hold
+no partial slices. Each tokenizer worker allows at most 64 pending publications,
+whose aligned payload bytes together cannot exceed its share of the pool.
+`SGLANG_MM_FEATURE_CACHE_MB` still controls the total pool across tokenizer
+workers; admission does not allocate another pool or change the processor backend.
+EPD and PD are not supported with this option.
+
+OpenAI and Native HTTP requests return `413 / mm_memory_request_too_large` when
+one batch cannot fit even in an empty pool, or `429 / mm_memory_overloaded` when
+the queue is full or the wait expires. Retry only the latter, with backoff.
+If streaming headers have already been sent, the error arrives as an SSE error
+event instead of a different HTTP status. Native Engine calls raise the corresponding
+`MmMemoryRequestTooLarge` or `MmMemoryOverloaded` exception.
+Native gRPC maps these to `INVALID_ARGUMENT` and `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, respectively.
+
+With `--enable-metrics`, inspect `sglang:mm_publication_requests_total`,
+`sglang:mm_publication_wait_seconds`, and `sglang:mm_publication_state` (pending
+count/bytes, occupied/free bytes, largest free range, and IPC free slots).
+Largest-free-range values are per-worker diagnostics; summing them does not
+describe a single allocation that can fit across workers.
+`sglang:mm_publication_oldest_lease_seconds` shows the oldest unreclaimed slice.
+The `mm_publication_reclaimed_total` and
+`mm_publication_reclaimed_lifetime_seconds_total` counters give the count and
+total lifetime of reclaimed slices (including rollback), not GPU copy time.
+`sglang:mm_publication_cpu_spills_total` stays zero on the guarded path: pressure
+waits or rejects rather than spilling. These observations use CPU bookkeeping;
+they do not add GPU synchronization to a metrics scrape.
+

 - **Use `--mm-process-config '{"image":{"max_pixels":1048576},"video":{"fps":3,"max_pixels":602112,"max_frames":60}}'`**: To set `image`, `video`, and `audio` input limits.
